_about: The spine manifest. Read by deploy/checks/check-orphans.mjs (Phase 0 T4); that file's header
documents the heuristics, their known blind spots, and the ORPHAN_GATE=block switch.
TWO LISTS, TWO JOBS:
structures — spine columns and types that are supposed to be load-bearing. The gate counts
production READERS for each. Zero readers is reported today and FAILS the build
from Phase 1 exit (ORPHAN_GATE=block). Phase 1/2 tasks APPEND their new spine
columns here in their own commits.
tables     — every table in the migration chain that carries an agent link AND a state column.
Declaring is mandatory and ALWAYS blocking, from day one: an undeclared one fails
the build. This is the machine check for the plan's own falsifier — 'work/tracker
unification producing a second system in practice' (DOJO-OVERHAUL-PLAN Part VI).
workShaped answers ONE question, the OR1 test: do these rows track a unit of work whose
completion someone is owed, keyed to an agent? A table whose migration text shows a terminal
state may NOT be declared workShaped:false — the checker refuses that. 'why' is required on
every entry; a declaration nobody explained is a rubber stamp.
waivers — {entry, reason, date} suppress a zero-reader report for ONE structure. They are
printed and counted on every run. More than 5 across Arc 1 is the pre-committed signal that the
RULE is wrong and the rule gets fixed. Waivers do NOT apply to the table rule: an undeclared
work-shaped table is fixed by declaring it, which costs one entry and one sentence.
Every reader count in the AS-BUILT notes was measured by this checker at HEAD 6895eda on
2026-07-27; `node deploy/checks/check-orphans.mjs --explain <id>` reproduces any of them.

structures.why: Origin spine: the root of the causal chain, so 'who ultimately asked for this' stops being re-derived from prose. Measured 2026-07-27: nothing in production reads it — and nothing writes it either. Every root_id in server source belongs to a DIFFERENT table (destructive_approvals, audit_log, deliveries, turns, inter_agent_messages, tool_receipts, router_log).

Origin spine: which task the message belongs to. Measured 2026-07-27: HAS a production reader (agent/v2/counterparty.ts selects it from messages), so it does not warn. Kept declared because it is a spine column Phase 1/2 must keep wired — this list is what must stay read, not a list of today's failures.

Voice identity (OR4): who actually spoke a persisted voice row — owner | caller | agent. Written by voice/session-record.ts; nothing reads it back, so spoken-turn attribution is still inferred elsewhere.
Binds a persisted row to the voice session that produced it. Same writer, same silence on the read side.

The typed spoken-stream lane on the turn record (voice | phone | null). Written by agent/v2/turn-record.ts on every turn open; no reader, so continuation context still cannot ask the record 'was this turn spoken?'.
Ties a delivery row to the tool receipt that produced it. Written by agent/v2/deliveries.ts; no reader. Phase 2 makes `work.done` require a delivery, which makes this link load-bearing.
Which delivery carried this artifact to the user. Measured 2026-07-27: the identifier does not appear in production source AT ALL — neither written nor read. The most orphaned of the eight.

The engine's declared nine-phase skeleton as a type. Phase 6's exit gate is 'TurnPhase is load-bearing (state transitions recorded per turn)'. Measured 2026-07-27: no file outside its own defining module mentions it — the skeleton is declared and unused, which is exactly what Phase 6 exists to fix.

tables.name: tasks
tables.why: THE tracker. OR1: this table evolves into the `work` spine (Phase 2) and keeps its ID space. Note for anyone extending the detector: it links agents through `assigned_to TEXT REFERENCES agents(id)`, NOT a column named agent_id — which is why the declaration trigger is the structural shape rather than the literal name.

tables.name: task_runs
tables.why: One row per execution of a task; part of the tasks family the plan names as partial work-tracking system #1. (It has never held a row in the live DB, and that is NOT evidence of deadness — rows are deleted with their tasks, and it has a live route, live UI and a conformance test: roadmap non-negotiable #15.)

tables.name: open_loops
tables.why: Structured unanswered obligations per agent (open | resolved | stale). Named in the plan as one of the five partial systems that each guess at 'is someone owed something'.
tables.disposition: Phase 2 — deleted; owner-attributed rows import as open `work` rows (Stable Bridge).

tables.name: generation_jobs
tables.why: Per-agent async media-generation queue: queued -> running -> succeeded | failed (services/generation-jobs.ts). Structurally a work tracker keyed to an agent, and NOT one of the five the plan enumerated — recorded here so Phase 2 decides deliberately instead of discovering it later.
tables.disposition: Undecided at Phase 0. Phase 2 judges whether it folds into `work` or stays a typed side-queue.

tables.name: video_jobs
tables.why: The same shape again for video: queued -> polling -> succeeded | failed | cancelled (services/video-job-poller.ts). Two independent job queues with the same lifecycle is the duplication pattern this project exists to stop.
tables.disposition: Undecided at Phase 0. Same Phase 2 judgement as generation_jobs.

tables.name: healer_proposals
tables.why: Proposed fixes awaiting the owner's decision: pending -> approved | denied, with resolved_at (gateway/routes/healer.ts). A queue of things someone is owed a decision on, keyed to an agent.
tables.disposition: Sweep F owns the healer; the approval-routing pattern is explicitly promoted, not deleted.

tables.name: destructive_approvals
tables.why: A non-primary agent's held destructive tool call, waiting on the primary's decision (agent/destructive-gate.ts). Short-lived, but it is a per-agent row with a terminal state that someone is owed an answer on — declared true rather than argued down.
tables.disposition: Phase 5 rebuilds permissions; the approval flow (exact command, once) is on the preserve list.

tables.name: agents
tables.why: The agent registry itself. `status` is a PROCESS lifecycle (idle | working | paused | error | terminated), not a unit of work, and the agent link the detector found is the self-referential spawn edge `parent_agent`. Caught by the structural trigger and declared not-work on purpose — the detector is deliberately over-eager.

tables.name: turns
tables.why: The turn record. `outcome` (answered | no_reply | parked | handoff | aborted | brake | error) says how a TURN ended, not whether an obligation is outstanding. A spine table in its own right (Part III).
tables.disposition: Stays and grows — turn identity allocated at turn start in Phase 2.

tables.name: deliveries
tables.why: The delivery ledger: one row per send attempt, `outcome` (delivered | failed | held) recording how the send went. It is the EVIDENCE a piece of work finished, not a second place where work is tracked.
tables.disposition: Stays and becomes universal in Phase 2 (recorded at the five transport doors).

tables.name: techniques
tables.why: An authored artifact, not a job. `state` is an editorial lifecycle (draft | review | published) on a document that has no completion anyone is owed.
tables.disposition: Sweep D — equip/export/import integrity; the table stays.

tables.name: twilio_call_log
tables.why: A transport log mirroring Twilio's own call status for a phone call that already happened. No work is claimed, assigned or completed here.
tables.disposition: Sweep B — voice/phone consolidation; the log stays.
